parties.ourParty: Verizon Owner Trust 2020-A, together with Verizon ABS LLC (Issuer and Depositor)
parties.counterparty: Cellco Partnership d/b/a Verizon Wireless (Servicer, Marketing Agent and Originator)

plans.note: Securitization TSAs typically limit the Servicer's/Marketing Agent's liability and disclaim liability for errors in judgment in the Servicer covenants/liability provisions of Article VI, with related exculpation possibly in Article X (Miscellaneous) and successor-servicer provisions of Article VII. Check for one-sided caps in favour of Cellco and absence of carve-outs for fraud, wilful misconduct, gross negligence and indemnity obligations.

Look for Servicer/Marketing Agent indemnification of the Issuer, Depositor, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee in Article VI (and any indemnity for Successor Servicer costs in Article VII; Asset Representations Reviewer indemnities near sec-p0441). Confirm indemnities run in our favour and are not capped or conditioned; note that IP-infringement indemnity is atypical for this deal type.

No restriction on the Issuer's or Depositor's business activity is expected; Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article X are the only plausible homes. Note that Permitted Activities limits on the Issuer arise under the Trust Agreement/structural covenants, not as a vendor non-compete, so do not flag those.

Check Article III (servicing appointment — exclusive appointment of Cellco as Servicer) and Article II for any obligation to source receivables solely from the Verizon Originators; a sole-servicer appointment is structural and generally not treated as a prohibited exclusivity on us.
No most-favoured-nation pricing construct is expected in a transfer and servicing agreement; scan Article IX and Article X only to confirm.
Employee non-solicit is unusual here; the closest analogue would be restrictions around hiring in the Successor Servicer transition provisions (Article VII) or Article IX.

Article VII governs Servicer resignation and termination (including Servicer Termination Events and our right to remove) and Article VIII governs termination of the agreement. Test whether Cellco can resign at will mid-term and whether our termination rights are conditioned on a Successor Servicer being appointed; also consider Optional Acquisition/Optional Redemption exit mechanics.
Term runs to termination of the Issuer/final payment on the Notes rather than by renewal cycle; confirm in Article VIII that there is no evergreen renewal or notice window before marking missing.

Governing law, submission to jurisdiction and waiver of jury trial should sit in Article X (Miscellaneous); New York is expected and acceptable. Also review the dispute resolution provisions at sec-p0441 (mediation/arbitration under the Arbitration Rules) for mandatory arbitration that displaces courts.

Expect assignment/successor provisions in Article X and merger-or-consolidation and 'no assignment of Servicer duties' covenants in Article VI. Confirm the Issuer/Depositor may assign to the Indenture Trustee and successors and that Cellco cannot terminate or refuse consent on our change of control.

Property rights here concern the Depositor Transferred Property, Receivable Files and Schedule of Receivables (Article II) and Servicer records/Personally Identifiable Information handling (Article III). Confirm records and data created in servicing are held for the Issuer and that no Customer data or IP is assigned to Cellco; a classic deliverables-IP clause is likely absent.

Check Article III/VII for any licence of Cellco systems, software or marks to a Successor Servicer; if present, test affiliate/contractor scope and revocability. Otherwise treat as absent for this deal type.

Audit-type rights run in our favour here (Regulation AB servicing assessments, Attestation Report, Compliance Statement and annual certification at sec-p1045; Asset Representations Review access to Review Materials at sec-p0441). Verify no reciprocal audit of the Issuer/Depositor at our cost; rights benefiting us should not be flagged.

Look for any fee uplift or penalty payable by the Issuer — e.g. Additional Successor Servicer Fee, Supplemental Servicing Fee or make-whole/Make-Whole Payment mechanics in Article IV/VII — and assess whether any charge functions as a penalty against us rather than compensation.

Eligibility Representations and Servicer/Originator representations sit in Article II with the reacquisition/acquisition remedy (Servicer Representation Obligation, Originator Reacquisition Obligation, sec-2.6) and the dispute resolution backstop at sec-p0441. Confirm the remedy is a real repurchase obligation and that survival is not time-limited in a way that defeats it.

Servicer insurance/fidelity bond covenants sometimes appear among the Servicer covenants in Article III or VI; if none exists, record as missing given Cellco handles Obligor Personally Identifiable Information.

Consider Additional Receivables acquisition mechanics and Acquisition Deposit/Negative Carry funding in Articles II and IV — these are structural funding obligations, not take-or-pay vendor commitments, so flag only if the Issuer is obliged to purchase regardless of eligibility with no exit.

Article VII should require the outgoing Servicer to cooperate with and deliver records, Receivable Files and Collections to the Successor Servicer; check the transition period, who bears transition costs (Additional Successor Servicer Fee) and delivery of data in usable form, with wind-down mechanics in Article VIII.
